newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in thin trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed narrowly mixed Thursday in thin trade as players were sidelined, disappointed that October's year-on-year gross domestic production (GDP) figure was negative, brokers said.
They said prices were likely to fall Friday as the market absorbed the news that October's 0.8 percent year-on-year GDP fall was the economy's first contraction since March.
Thursday, the General Index dipped 0.13 percent to 1,438.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 0.18 percent to 2,038.6 points, according to preliminary figures.
In a total of 1,068 trades, volume was estimated at 26.7 million soles ($10.3 million).

While the market had in part already absorbed the expectation that October's year-on-year gross domestic product figure would not be encouraging, investors were surprised that the economy actually suffered a contraction, brokers said.
"The GDP figure is very weak. We were expecting flat growth at least," said Hector Neyra of local brokerage Provalor.
Thursday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed stable at 5.09 soles in volume of 718,000 shares, according to preliminary figures.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, in which the government is selling a 30 percent stake this month, closed down 1.15 percent at 3.45 soles in volume of 54,000 shares.
